items.title: Finite discounted MDP with bounded real rewards
items.exact_statement_or_definition:
Let $S$ be a nonempty finite set, let $A(s)$ be a nonempty finite set for each $s\in S$, and let $D=\{(s,a):s\in S,\ a\in A(s)\}$. Here **finite** means bijective with a natural number. Put $S_0=|S|$ and $A_0=\max_{s\in S}|A(s)|$. Fix a discount $0\le\gamma<1$. Give $S$ and $D$ their discrete sigma-algebras and give $[0,1]$ its Borel sigma-algebra. A **bounded-reward finite discounted Markov decision process** is a probability kernel $K$ from $D$ to $S\times[0,1]$. At pair $(s,a)$, $K(\cdot\mid s,a)$ is the joint law of the next state and the reward; these two coordinates need not be independent. Define the state-transition probabilities and expected rewards by

$$P(s'\mid s,a)=K(\{s'\}\times[0,1]\mid s,a),\qquad r(s,a)=\int_{S\times[0,1]}\rho\,K(ds',d\rho\mid s,a).$$

A **history-dependent behavior** is a sequence of probability kernels from observed-history spaces $H_t$ to the finite action alphabet $\mathcal A=\bigcup_{s\in S}A(s)$, assigning probability zero to actions outside $A(s_t)$ at every history ending in state $s_t$. Here $H_t$ consists of histories $(s_0,a_0,R_1,s_1,\ldots,a_{t-1},R_t,s_t)$, with discrete sigma-algebras on finite state/action coordinates and the Borel sigma-algebra on each reward coordinate; it has the resulting finite-product sigma-algebra. A **stationary Markov policy** assigns one distribution on $A(s)$ to each state, independently of earlier history. During interaction, after choosing $a_t$ in state $s_t$, the next pair $(s_{t+1},R_{t+1})$ is drawn from $K(\cdot\mid s_t,a_t)$.

items.title: Well-defined discounted values and optimal Bellman fixed points
items.exact_statement_or_definition:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. In every bounded-reward finite discounted Markov decision process with nonempty finite state set $S$, nonempty finite action sets $A(s)$, and $0\le\gamma<1$, the trajectory law of every history-dependent behavior from every starting state exists. Its discounted return is measurable, integrable, and between $0$ and $1/(1-\gamma)$. For each stationary policy $\pi$, its value $V^\pi$ satisfies its Bellman equation. The optimality operator

$$T^*V(s)=\max_{a\in A(s)}\left[r(s,a)+\gamma\sum_{s'\in S}P(s'\mid s,a)V(s')\right]$$

is a $\gamma$ contraction in the supremum norm, meaning $\|T^*V-T^*W\|_\infty\le\gamma\|V-W\|_\infty$ for all $V,W:S\to\mathbb R$, where $\|V\|_\infty=\max_{s\in S}|V(s)|$, and has a unique fixed point $V^*$. This fixed point is the supremum of the values of all history-dependent behaviors and is attained by a deterministic stationary greedy policy. The optimal action value is

$$Q^*(s,a)=r(s,a)+\gamma\sum_{s'\in S}P(s'\mid s,a)V^*(s'),$$

and $V^*(s)=\max_{a\in A(s)}Q^*(s,a)$ with $Q^*(s,a)\ge0$.

items.title: Concentration for adaptively sampled MDP observations
items.exact_statement_or_definition:
Assume AC and fix a bounded-reward finite discounted MDP with state set $S$. For each admissible pair $(s,a)$, let $(S'_i,R_i)_{i\ge1}$ be an independent potential stream with common joint law $K(\cdot\mid s,a)$; an interaction reveals the next unused sample from that pair's stream only when the pair is visited. This construction has the same finite-trajectory law as interaction with the MDP under any history-dependent behavior. For a fixed pair and $m\ge1$, its reward samples satisfy
$$\mathbb P\!\left(\left|\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m R_i-r(s,a)\right|>x\right)\le 2e^{-2mx^2}\qquad(x>0).$$
If $\widehat P_m$ is the empirical distribution of $S'_1,\ldots,S'_m$ and $P(\cdot\mid s,a)$ is the true next-state marginal, then
$$\mathbb E\|\widehat P_m-P(\cdot\mid s,a)\|_1\le\sqrt{\frac{|S|}{m}},\qquad \mathbb P\!\left(\|\widehat P_m-P(\cdot\mid s,a)\|_1>\sqrt{\frac{|S|}{m}}+\sqrt{\frac{2\ln(1/\delta)}{m}}\right)\le\delta\quad(0<\delta<1),$$
where $\|q\|_1=\sum_{s'\in S}|q(s')|$ and $\ln$ is the natural logarithm.
More generally, for a filtration $(\mathcal F_i)_{i=0}^m$, if $Y_i$ is $\mathcal F_i$-measurable, $0\le Y_i\le B$, and $\mu_i=\mathbb E[Y_i\mid\mathcal F_{i-1}]$, then
$$\mathbb P\!\left(\left|\sum_{i=1}^m(Y_i-\mu_i)\right|\ge mx\right)\le2e^{-2mx^2/B^2}\qquad(B>0,\ x>0).$$
No independence between reward and next state within a single transition is assumed. The confidence bounds are for a fixed deterministic sample size or a fixed-size batch; this item makes no uniform confidence claim at a data-dependent sample count. At a finite history-dependent visit count, the next fixed number of unused potential outcomes still has its conditional iid law.

items.title: PAC-MDP sample complexity of exploration
items.exact_statement_or_definition:
Assume AC, fix a bounded-reward finite discounted MDP, an initial state, and a learning algorithm whose behavior is a history-dependent policy. At time $t\ge1$, let $h_t$ be the observed history ending at state $s_t$. The continuation behavior $A_t$ is the tail of the algorithm's action kernels after $h_t$, and $V^{A_t}(h_t)$ is the expected discounted return of the continuation process generated from that fixed history by those tail kernels. Set $S=|S|$ and $A=\max_{s\in S}|A(s)|$.
For $\epsilon\ge0$, the $\epsilon$-bad-step count is
$$N_\epsilon=\#\{t\ge1:V^{A_t}(h_t)<V^*(s_t)-\epsilon\},$$
where the count may be infinite. For $\epsilon>0$ and $0<\delta<1$, a PAC-MDP bound is a specified finite function $B(S,A,\epsilon,\delta,\gamma)$ such that, for every MDP with these finite state/action sizes and every initial state, $\mathbb P(N_\epsilon\le B(S,A,\epsilon,\delta,\gamma))\ge1-\delta$. This definition does not require the bad steps to precede a permanent stopping time.

items.title: Admissible upper heuristic for a discounted MDP
items.exact_statement_or_definition: For a bounded-reward finite discounted MDP, an **admissible upper heuristic** is a function $U:D\to[0,V_0]$ such that $Q^*(s,a)\le U(s,a)$ for every admissible pair and a supplied scalar satisfies $0\le V_0\le(1-\gamma)^{-1}$. Define the effective reward-scale cap $V_{\max}=\max\{1,V_0\}$. Then $U(s,a)\le V_{\max}\le(1-\gamma)^{-1}$. The floor at $1$ is part of this convention because an observed reward can lie anywhere in $[0,1]$, even when the heuristic values are all smaller than $1$.

items.title: Value stability under empirical model error
items.exact_statement_or_definition:
Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be bounded-reward finite discounted MDPs on the same finite state set $S$ and the same admissible action sets, with common discount $0\le\gamma<1$. Write $r_i,P_i,V_i^\pi,V_i^*$ for their mean rewards, transition laws, stationary-policy values, and optimal values. Suppose $0\le V_i^\pi(s),V_i^*(s)\le V$ for every state, model index $i$, and stationary policy $\pi$, and that for every admissible pair
$$|r_1(s,a)-r_2(s,a)|\le\alpha,\qquad \|P_1(\cdot\mid s,a)-P_2(\cdot\mid s,a)\|_1\le\beta.$$
For finite vectors, $\|v\|_\infty=\max_{s\in S}|v(s)|$ and $\|p\|_1=\sum_{s\in S}|p(s)|$.
Then every common stationary policy and the optimal values satisfy
$$\|V_1^\pi-V_2^\pi\|_\infty\le\frac{\alpha+\gamma V\beta}{1-\gamma},\qquad \|V_1^*-V_2^*\|_\infty\le\frac{\alpha+\gamma V\beta}{1-\gamma}.$$
There is also a trap-model form that does not assume a tight cap for the second model: for $W>0$, suppose all stationary-policy and optimal values in $M_1$ are at most $2W$, all rewards in $M_2$ lie in $[0,1]$, and $\gamma\beta\le(1-\gamma)/2$. Then every common stationary policy and the optimal values satisfy
$$\|V_1^\pi-V_2^\pi\|_\infty\le\frac{2(\alpha+2\gamma W\beta)}{1-\gamma},\qquad \|V_1^*-V_2^*\|_\infty\le\frac{2(\alpha+2\gamma W\beta)}{1-\gamma}.$$

items.title: Known-state/action MDP with optimistic self-loops
items.exact_statement_or_definition: Let $M$ be a bounded-reward finite discounted MDP with discount $\gamma$, let $K\subseteq D$ be a set of known state-action pairs, and let $q:D\to[0,V_{\max}]$ with $V_{\max}\le(1-\gamma)^{-1}$. The **known-state/action MDP** $M_K(q)$ agrees with $M$ on every pair in $K$. For each pair $(s,a)\notin K$, add a distinct absorbing state $\bot_{s,a}$ with one admissible action. The unknown pair transitions deterministically to $\bot_{s,a}$ and gives deterministic reward $(1-\gamma)q(s,a)$; the sink action self-loops with the same deterministic reward $(1-\gamma)q(s,a)$. These rewards lie in $[0,1]$. The sink state's value is $q(s,a)$, so the unknown pair's Bellman backup is exactly $(1-\gamma)q(s,a)+\gamma q(s,a)=q(s,a)$, independent of the value function on the original states.

items.title: R-MAX with an admissible heuristic
items.exact_statement_or_definition:
**Input:** A bounded-reward finite discounted MDP interaction, its discount $0\le\gamma<1$, an admissible upper heuristic $U$ with cap $V_{\max}$, an integer sample threshold $m\ge1$, a value-iteration error tolerance $0<\beta<(1-\gamma)^{-1}$, and a fixed total order on each finite action set. Write $\ln$ for the natural logarithm.

**Output:** At each interaction time $t$, the selected action $a_t$. The action-value table $Q$, known set, sample lists, and empirical model are internal state; the procedure does not return $Q$ as an output.

Initialize each pair as unknown, set $Q(s,a)=U(s,a)$, and give each pair an empty list of observed rewards and next states. For interaction times $t=1,2,\ldots$, in the current state choose a maximizing action using the fixed tie order, output and take that action $a_t$, and observe reward $R_{t+1}$ and next state $S_{t+1}$. If the pair is unknown, append this observation until its list has length $m$. When it reaches $m$, mark the pair known, set its empirical reward to the sample mean and its empirical transition law to the sample frequencies. Rebuild all action values by setting the working table $Q^{(0)}(s,a)=0$, then for $j=0,\ldots,L-1$ setting $Q^{(j+1)}=H_KQ^{(j)}$, and finally replacing $Q$ by $Q^{(L)}$, for the operator
$$H_KQ(s,a)=\begin{cases}\widehat r(s,a)+\gamma\sum_{s'}\widehat P(s'\mid s,a)\max_{b\in A(s')}Q(s',b),&(s,a)\in K,\\ U(s,a),&(s,a)\notin K,\end{cases}$$
where $K$ is the current known set and
$$L=\max\!\left\{1,\left\lceil\frac{\ln(1/[\beta(1-\gamma)])}{1-\gamma}\right\rceil\right\}.$$
Pairs and their samples are never removed from $K$ or discarded. After processing the observation and any rebuild, use the observed $S_{t+1}$ as the current state in the next iteration. The algorithm specifies no computational-time bound.

items.title: Delayed Q-learning with an admissible heuristic
items.exact_statement_or_definition:
**Input:** A bounded-reward finite discounted MDP interaction, its discount $0\le\gamma<1$, an admissible upper heuristic $U$ with cap $V_{\max}$, an integer batch size $m\ge1$, a bonus $0<\epsilon_1<1$, and a fixed total order on each action set.

**Output:** At each interaction time $t$, the selected action $a_t$. The table $Q$, batch sums, sample counts, batch-start times, learning flags, and global last-update time are internal state; the procedure does not return them as outputs.

Initialize $Q(s,a)=U(s,a)$, batch sum $B(s,a)=0$, sample count $\ell(s,a)=0$, batch start $b(s,a)=0$, learning flag $L(s,a)=\mathrm{true}$, and global last-update time $t^*=0$. For interaction times $t=1,2,\ldots$, in current state $s$, choose an action maximizing $Q(s,\cdot)$ under the fixed tie order, output and take that action $a_t$, then observe reward $r$ and next state $s'$. If $b(s,a)\le t^*$, set $L(s,a)=\mathrm{true}$. If $L(s,a)$ is true, set $b(s,a)=t$ when $\ell(s,a)=0$, increment $\ell(s,a)$ by one, and add $r+\gamma\max_{c\in A(s')}Q(s',c)$ to $B(s,a)$. When $\ell(s,a)=m$, set $\bar B=B(s,a)/m$. If $Q(s,a)-\bar B\ge2\epsilon_1$, replace $Q(s,a)$ by $\bar B+\epsilon_1$ and set $t^*=t$. Otherwise set $L(s,a)=\mathrm{false}$ exactly when $b(s,a)>t^*$. In either outcome reset $B(s,a)=0$ and $\ell(s,a)=0$ after a completed batch; if $L(s,a)$ remains false, make no sample or Q update on this visit. Leave all other entries unchanged. Use $s'$ as the current state in the next iteration.

items.title: Escape-event reduction for optimistic greedy learning
items.exact_statement_or_definition:
Assume AC. Let a learning algorithm interact with a bounded-reward finite discounted MDP. Suppose constants $B,W,Q_c$ satisfy $0<B$, $0<W\le(1-\gamma)^{-1}$, $0<Q_c\le(1-\gamma)^{-1}$, and $V^*(s)\le B$. The learner maintains $0\le Q_t(s,a)\le Q_c$ and, whenever $(s,a)\notin K_t$, $Q_t(s,a)\le W$. Put $V_t(s)=\max_{a\in A(s)}Q_t(s,a)$, and let $\pi_t$ be the deterministic greedy policy under a fixed tie order. Before acting at time $t$, let $K_t$ be a history-measurable set of known pairs; assume it stays fixed until a Q-value update or a selection of a pair outside $K_t$. Write $M_t=M_{K_t}(Q_t)$ for the known-state/action MDP and $C=B+W$. For parameters $0<\eta\le C$ with $\eta(1-\gamma)<1$ and $0<\rho<1/2$, suppose that with probability at least $1-\rho$, simultaneously for every $t,s$,
$$V_t(s)\ge V^*(s)-\eta,\qquad V_t(s)-V^{\pi_t}_{M_t}(s)\le\eta,$$
and the total number of Q-update times plus outside-$K_t$ selection times is at most a finite real $\zeta\ge0$. Define $q=\eta/(2C)$, set
$$H=\begin{cases}1,&\gamma=0,\\ \max\{1,\lceil \ln(1/[\eta(1-\gamma)])/(-\ln\gamma)\rceil\},&0<\gamma<1,\end{cases}\qquad M=\left\lceil\frac{2(\zeta+1)+2\ln(1/\rho)}{q}\right\rceil.$$
Then, with probability at least $1-2\rho$, the PAC-MDP count satisfies $N_{4\eta}\le HM$. Here $\ln$ is the natural logarithm.

items.title: Adaptive empirical-model accuracy for R-MAX
items.exact_statement_or_definition:
Let $M$ be a bounded-reward finite discounted MDP, let $0<\eta<V_{\max}/4$ and $0<\delta<1$, and let $U,V_{\max}$ be an admissible heuristic with $V_{\max}=\max\{1,V_0\}$. Put
$$b=\frac{\eta(1-\gamma)}{64V_{\max}},\quad L_0=\ln\frac{8SA}{\delta},\quad m=\left\lceil\frac{8(S+L_0)}{b^2}\right\rceil,\quad \beta=\frac{\eta(1-\gamma)}{16},$$
where $S=|S|$ and $A=\max_s|A(s)|$. Run R-MAX with this sample threshold and approximation tolerance. For $K_t$ the current known set, let $\widehat M_{K_t}$ use its empirical laws on $K_t$ and the heuristic absorbing states elsewhere, and let $M_{K_t}=M_{K_t}(U)$ use the true laws on $K_t$. Define $E_\eta=\{(s,a):U(s,a)\ge V^*(s)-\eta\}$. With probability at least $1-\delta$, simultaneously at all times: every stationary-policy value in $\widehat M_{K_t}$ differs from its value in $M_{K_t}$ by at most $\eta/8$; the current action values satisfy $\|Q_t-Q^*_{\widehat M_{K_t}}\|_\infty\le\beta$ and $0\le Q_t(s,a)\le(1-\gamma)^{-1}$; the greedy value obeys $V_t(s)\ge V^*(s)-\eta$; and $V_t(s)-V^{\pi_t}_{M_{K_t}}(s)\le\eta$ for every state. On this event, the total number of value-table rebuilds plus selections of pairs outside $K_t$ is at most $(m+1)|E_\eta|$.

items.title: Delayed Q-learning optimism and update-count bounds
items.exact_statement_or_definition:
Fix a bounded-reward finite discounted MDP, an admissible heuristic with cap $V_{\max}$, and $0<\epsilon_1<1$. Put $D(s,a)=[U(s,a)-V^*(s)]_+$, $\kappa=\lceil SA V_{\max}/\epsilon_1\rceil$, $N=SA(1+\kappa)$, and $C_1=1+\gamma V_{\max}$. Run Delayed Q-learning with a positive integer $m$ satisfying
$$m\ge\left\lceil\frac{C_1^2}{2\epsilon_1^2}\ln\frac{8N}{\delta}\right\rceil\qquad(0<\delta<1).$$
For $V_t(s)=\max_aQ_t(s,a)$, define
$$K_t=\left\{(s,a):Q_t(s,a)-\left(r(s,a)+\gamma\sum_{s'}P(s'\mid s,a)V_t(s')\right)\le3\epsilon_1\right\}.$$
With probability at least $1-\delta$, all estimates remain optimistic, $Q_t(s,a)\ge Q^*(s,a)$ for every $t,s,a$; every attempted update whose first sample is taken with its pair outside $K_t$ succeeds; the number of successful updates is at most
$$G=\sum_{s,a}\left(1+\frac{D(s,a)}{\epsilon_1}\right);$$
and the number of visits selecting a pair outside $K_t$ is at most $2mG$. The additive $1$ in each pair's update allowance is necessary, including when $U(s,a)=V^*(s)$.

items.title: PAC-MDP sample complexity of R-MAX
items.exact_statement_or_definition:
Let $M$ be a bounded-reward finite discounted MDP, write $S=|S|$ and $A=\max_s|A(s)|$, and fix $0\le\epsilon<(1-\gamma)^{-1}$, $0<\delta<1$, and an admissible heuristic with normalized cap $V_{\max}$. At $\epsilon=0$, if $V^*(s)=0$ at every state then $N_0=0$; no finite zero-tolerance extension holds uniformly over this class: already at $\gamma=0$, every fixed finite legal sample threshold $m$ and value-iteration tolerance $\beta$ admits an admissible one-state example for R-MAX with $N_0=\infty$ with positive probability. This does not assert failure for every fixed heuristic or model. The parameter formulas below are evaluated only when $\epsilon>0$. Assume now $\epsilon>0$. If $\epsilon\ge V_{\max}$, then $N_\epsilon=0$. Otherwise put
$$\eta=\epsilon/4,\quad b=\frac{\eta(1-\gamma)}{64V_{\max}},\quad m=\left\lceil\frac{8(S+\ln(16SA/\delta))}{b^2}\right\rceil,\quad \beta=\frac{\eta(1-\gamma)}{16},$$
and run R-MAX with sample threshold $m$ and value-iteration tolerance $\beta$. Let $E_\eta=\{(s,a):U(s,a)\ge V^*(s)-\eta\}$ and $\zeta=(m+1)|E_\eta|$. Define $q=\eta/(4V_{\max})$, and define $H$ and $M$ by
$$H=\begin{cases}1,&\gamma=0,\\ \max\{1,\lceil\ln(1/[\eta(1-\gamma)])/(-\ln\gamma)\rceil\},&0<\gamma<1,\end{cases}\qquad M=\left\lceil\frac{2(\zeta+1)+2\ln(2/\delta)}q\right\rceil.$$
Then $\mathbb P(N_\epsilon\le HM)\ge1-\delta$. For the uninformative heuristic $U(s,a)=V_{\max}=(1-\gamma)^{-1}$, the bound is $\widetilde O(S^2A/[\epsilon^3(1-\gamma)^6])$, where $\widetilde O$ suppresses logarithmic factors.

items.title: PAC-MDP sample complexity of Delayed Q-learning
items.exact_statement_or_definition:
Let $M$ be a bounded-reward finite discounted MDP, write $S=|S|$ and $A=\max_s|A(s)|$, and fix $0\le\epsilon<(1-\gamma)^{-1}$, $0<\delta<1$, and an admissible heuristic with normalized cap $V_{\max}$. At $\epsilon=0$, if $V^*(s)=0$ at every state then $N_0=0$; no finite zero-tolerance extension holds uniformly over this class: already at $\gamma=0$, every fixed finite legal batch size $m$ and bonus $\epsilon_1$ admits an admissible one-state example for Delayed Q-learning with $N_0=\infty$ with positive probability. This does not assert failure for every fixed heuristic or model. The parameter formulas below are evaluated only when $\epsilon>0$. Assume now $\epsilon>0$. If $\epsilon\ge V_{\max}$, then $N_\epsilon=0$. Otherwise put
$$\eta=\epsilon/4,\quad \epsilon_1=\frac{\eta(1-\gamma)}3,\quad \kappa=\left\lceil\frac{SA V_{\max}}{\epsilon_1}\right\rceil,\quad N=SA(1+\kappa),\quad C_1=1+\gamma V_{\max},$$
and choose
$$m=\left\lceil\frac{C_1^2}{2\epsilon_1^2}\ln\frac{16N}{\delta}\right\rceil.$$
Run Delayed Q-learning with $m$ and $\epsilon_1$. Write $D(s,a)=[U(s,a)-V^*(s)]_+$, $G=\sum_{s,a}(1+D(s,a)/\epsilon_1)$, and $\zeta=\lceil(2m+1)G\rceil$. Define $q,H,M$ by
$$q=\frac{\eta}{4V_{\max}},\qquad H=\begin{cases}1,&\gamma=0,\\ \max\{1,\lceil\ln(1/[\eta(1-\gamma)])/(-\ln\gamma)\rceil\},&0<\gamma<1,\end{cases}\qquad M=\left\lceil\frac{2(\zeta+1)+2\ln(2/\delta)}q\right\rceil.$$
Then $\mathbb P(N_\epsilon\le HM)\ge1-\delta$. Equivalently, up to logarithmic factors, the bound is
$$\widetilde O\!\left(\frac{V_{\max}(1+\gamma V_{\max})^2\left[\sum_{s,a}D(s,a)+SA\epsilon(1-\gamma)\right]}{\epsilon^4(1-\gamma)^4}\right),$$
where $\widetilde O$ suppresses logarithmic factors. The additive term remains when all heuristic slacks vanish. For $V_{\max}=(1-\gamma)^{-1}$ this gives $\widetilde O(SA/[\epsilon^4(1-\gamma)^8])$.

items.title: The zero-tolerance boundary of PAC-MDP exploration
items.exact_statement_or_definition:
Assume AC, and use the history-conditioned bad-step count $N_\epsilon$ for bounded-reward finite discounted MDPs. The endpoint $\epsilon=0$ has the following properties.

1. Fix any single learning rule whose action kernels depend only on its observed history and common supplied inputs, not on the unknown MDP reward means. For every finite real $B\ge0$ and $0<\delta<1/2$, some one-state, two-action MDP with $\gamma=0$, Bernoulli rewards and the common admissible heuristic $U(a)=U(b)=V_{\max}=1$ satisfies $\mathbb P(N_0>B)>\delta$. Thus no finite bound depending only on state/action sizes, confidence and discount can hold uniformly at zero tolerance, even allowing randomized history-dependent learners.
2. For R-MAX, fix any integer $m\ge1$, $0<\beta<1$, and a tie order selecting $a$ first. For each $0<p<1$, take one state, $\gamma=0$, $U(a)=U(b)=V_{\max}=1$, reward $a\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)$ and deterministic reward $b=p/2$. Then $\mathbb P(N_0=\infty)\ge(1-p)^m$. For every $0<\delta<1$, some $p$ makes this probability exceed $\delta$; no fixed finite legal sample threshold gives a uniform finite zero-tolerance bound.
3. For Delayed Q-learning, fix any integer $m\ge1$, $0<\epsilon_1<1$, and a tie order selecting $b$ first. In the one-state model with $\gamma=0$, $U(a)=U(b)=V_{\max}=1$ and deterministic rewards $a=1$, $b=1-\epsilon_1$, the algorithm chooses $b$ forever and $N_0=\infty$ with probability one.
4. If $V^*(s)=0$ at every state of any bounded-reward finite discounted MDP, then every behavior has $N_0=0$. The impossibility is a uniform assertion over unknown models, not a claim that zero-tolerance behavior must always fail.

All models in clauses1–3 have nonempty finite state/action sets, rewards in $[0,1]$, and an admissible normalized cap. No parameter formula that divides by $\epsilon$ is evaluated at zero.

items.title: A finite bad-step count need not be a permanent stopping time
items.exact_statement_or_definition: Consider a one-state MDP with $\gamma=0$ and two actions $a,b$ whose deterministic rewards are $1,0$, respectively. For an integer $n\ge1$, let a deterministic history-dependent controller choose $b$ at times $1,\ldots,n$ and $n+2$, and choose $a$ at every other time. For $\epsilon=1/2$, it has exactly $n+1$ bad steps, including one after a good step.

items.title: An inadmissible heuristic can suppress exploration forever
items.exact_statement_or_definition: Consider a one-state MDP with $\gamma=0$ and actions $a,b$ having deterministic rewards $1,0$. Run the R-MAX procedure outside its admissibility guarantee with the inadmissible heuristic $U(a)=U(b)=0$, supplied scalar $V_0=0$ (so $V_{\max}=1$), tolerance $\beta=1/2$, any integer threshold $m\ge1$, and a tie order that selects $b$ first. It observes only $b$, chooses $b$ forever, and is $1/2$-bad at every time.

items.title: The uninformative heuristic exposes the discount-factor powers
items.exact_statement_or_definition:
Set $U(s,a)=V_{\max}=(1-\gamma)^{-1}$ for every pair, and let $0<\epsilon<(1-\gamma)^{-1}$. Then every pair belongs to $E_{\epsilon/4}$, and
$$\sum_{s,a}[U(s,a)-V^*(s)]_+\le\frac{SA}{1-\gamma}.$$
Substitution into the proved theorems gives the leading orders $\widetilde O(S^2A/[\epsilon^3(1-\gamma)^6])$ for R-MAX and $\widetilde O(SA/[\epsilon^4(1-\gamma)^8])$ for Delayed Q-learning.

items.title: Zero heuristic slack can still require one Delayed Q-learning update
items.exact_statement_or_definition: Consider a one-state MDP with $\gamma=0$ and actions $a,b$ of deterministic rewards $1,0$. Set $U(a)=U(b)=V^*(s)=V_{\max}=1$, use a tie order selecting $b$ first, and take any integer $m\ge1$ and $0<\epsilon_1<1/2$. Delayed Q-learning selects $b$ for its first $m$ samples and then lowers $Q(s,b)$, even though $\sum_{s,a}[U(s,a)-V^*(s)]_+=0$. In the PAC bound the resulting finite cost is covered by the additive $SA\epsilon(1-\gamma)$ term.
